meta.titre: Seed Germination: Conditions, Experiments and Changes
meta.sous_theme: What a seed needs and how to prove it

sections.contenu_markdown: A farmer in Bafoussam sows beans at the start of the rains. Some seeds sprout in a few days, while seeds left in a dry bag stay unchanged for months. Why does the same seed behave so differently? Germination is a favourite topic at the GCE because it can be tested by simple experiments, and examiners like to ask why each part of a set-up is there. This course gives you the conditions, the reasons behind them and the way to explain an experiment.

items: A seed contains an embryo and a store of food.
Respiration releases energy from food, and aerobic respiration uses oxygen.
Enzymes are proteins that speed up reactions, and they work best at a suitable temperature.

sections.titre: What a seed needs and why
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Parts of a seed
A seed has a protective **testa**, a small pore called the **micropyle**, and an **embryo** made of a **radicle** (future root) and a **plumule** (future shoot). One or two **cotyledons** store food.

### Conditions for germination
| Condition | Why the seed needs it |
|---|---|
| Water | Softens the testa and swells the seed. It activates enzymes and dissolves the digested food so that it can reach the embryo. |
| Oxygen | Needed for aerobic respiration, which releases the energy for growth. |
| Suitable temperature | Enzymes work best in warmth. Cold slows them down and great heat destroys them. |

Light is not needed by most seeds, and soil is not needed either, because the food comes from the seed itself.

### What happens inside
Enzymes change stored starch, protein and fat into soluble substances such as sugars and amino acids. These pass to the embryo for respiration and growth. The radicle emerges first and grows downwards. The plumule follows and grows upwards. At first the dry mass of the seedling falls, because stored food is used up in respiration. It rises again only when the seedling has green leaves and can photosynthesize.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must show that one condition is necessary
variantes.contenu_markdown: Change one factor only and keep the others the same. The control tube has water, air and warmth. Water: a second tube has dry cotton wool. Oxygen: a tube whose air is stripped of oxygen. Pyrogallic acid in alkali is used for this purpose, because **it absorbs oxygen from the air in the container**. Another method uses boiled and cooled water, which holds little dissolved air, topped with a layer of oil. Temperature: a tube kept in a refrigerator. Only the control germinates.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question mentions a thermometer, a flask or a disinfectant
variantes.contenu_markdown: Germinating seeds respire, and respiration releases heat. Put soaked, germinating seeds in a flask with a thermometer and plug it with cotton wool. Set up a control flask with seeds killed by boiling. The seeds are first soaked briefly in a disinfectant such as sodium oxochlorate(I) to kill bacteria and fungi on their surface. Those microbes would also respire and give out heat, which would spoil the result. The thermometer in the living seeds reads higher than the control.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question compares two seedlings
variantes.contenu_markdown: In **epigeal** germination the cotyledons are lifted above the ground, as in the French bean. In **hypogeal** germination they stay below the soil, as in maize.

sections.enonce_markdown: Describe an experiment to show that bean seeds need water to germinate. Say how you would make it a fair test and what result you expect.

etapes.action: Decide the single factor to change.
etapes.justification: A fair test changes one factor only. Here the factor is water.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Test tube A is kept moist and tube B is kept dry.

etapes.justification: The tubes must hold the same material so that only water differs.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Put the same number of bean seeds on cotton wool in each tube. Keep A moist and leave B dry.

etapes.action: Keep every other factor the same.
etapes.justification: Oxygen and warmth must be present in both, otherwise a failure to germinate could have another cause.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Both tubes are left open to the air in the same warm room.

etapes.action: State the expected result after a few days.
etapes.justification: Tube A is the control and tube B is the test.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The seeds in A germinate. The seeds in B do not.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** Place the same number of bean seeds on cotton wool in two test tubes, A and B. Keep the cotton wool in A moist and leave B dry. Leave both tubes open to the air in the same warm room, so that oxygen and temperature are the same. After a few days the seeds in A have germinated and the seeds in B have not. Since water was the only factor that differed, water is necessary for germination.

items.pourquoi_faux: Most seeds germinate in darkness, and many are buried in soil when they sprout.
items.correction_markdown: Water, oxygen and a suitable temperature are the needed conditions. Light is needed later, for photosynthesis by the seedling.

items.erreur_markdown: Germinating seeds take their food from the soil and make it by photosynthesis.
items.pourquoi_faux: The seedling has no green leaves at first. It lives on food stored in the seed.
items.correction_markdown: The embryo uses the food in the cotyledons or endosperm. Photosynthesis begins only when green leaves open.

items.erreur_markdown: The plumule comes out of the seed before the radicle.
items.pourquoi_faux: The root must anchor the seedling and absorb water first.
items.correction_markdown: The radicle emerges first and grows downwards. The plumule grows upwards afterwards.

items.erreur_markdown: Water gives the seed the energy to grow.
items.pourquoi_faux: Water carries substances and activates enzymes, but it holds no usable energy.
items.correction_markdown: The energy comes from respiration of stored food, which needs oxygen.

items.erreur_markdown: Pyrogallic acid is added to give the seeds more oxygen.
items.pourquoi_faux: It does the opposite. Its role is to remove oxygen.
items.correction_markdown: Pyrogallic acid absorbs oxygen from the air in the container, so the seeds are tested without oxygen.

items.enonce_markdown: Name three conditions needed for germination and state one use of each in the seed. Name one thing the seed does not need.
items.solution_markdown: **Water:** it softens the testa and dissolves digested food. **Oxygen:** it is used for respiration to release energy. **A suitable temperature:** it lets enzymes work at a good rate. Light is not needed (or soil).

items.enonce_markdown: Four tubes each contain the same number of dry seeds. P: moist cotton wool, 25°C, kept in a dark cupboard. Q: seeds completely covered with boiled, cooled water topped with oil, 25°C. R: moist cotton wool, kept in a refrigerator. S: dry cotton wool, 25°C. Predict which seeds germinate and give a reason for each result.
items.solution_markdown: **P germinates:** it has water, air and warmth, and light is not needed. **Q does not germinate:** boiling removed dissolved air and the oil keeps air out, so there is no oxygen for respiration. **R does not germinate, or does so very slowly:** the low temperature slows down the enzymes. **S does not germinate:** there is no water to activate the enzymes.

items.enonce_markdown: A student weighs the dry mass of a batch of germinating bean seedlings grown in darkness: 10.0 g at the start, 9.2 g after 3 days and 8.1 g after 6 days. (a) Calculate the percentage fall in dry mass over the 6 days. (b) Explain why the dry mass falls. (c) What would you expect to happen to the dry mass if the seedlings were later given light and developed green leaves?
items.solution_markdown: (a) Fall = 10.0 - 8.1 = 1.9 g. Percentage = 1.9 / 10.0 x 100 = **19%**. (b) The seedling cannot photosynthesize in darkness and has no green leaves. It uses stored food in respiration, and carbon is lost from the seedling as carbon dioxide, so the dry mass falls. (c) Once green leaves have formed, photosynthesis makes new food, so the dry mass **stops falling and starts to rise**.

items_markdown: Germination needs water, oxygen and a suitable temperature. Most seeds need neither light nor soil.
Water softens the testa and activates enzymes. Oxygen is used for respiration. Warmth lets enzymes work.
Experiments change one factor only and keep a control. Pyrogallic acid absorbs oxygen.
Germinating seeds release heat from respiration. Disinfecting the seeds removes microbes that would also give out heat.
The radicle emerges first and the plumule second. Dry mass falls at first and rises only once photosynthesis begins.
